title: Two Men Were Found Dead On A Brazilian Hillside Wearing Lead Masks. Nobody Knows Why.
description:
In 1966, two electronics technicians were found dead outside Rio de Janeiro, dressed in suits and wearing handmade lead masks over their eyes. Investigators never determined how they died.

#shorts #truestory #unsolvedmystery
sources: Dangerous Minds' account, "Be at the specified location: The baffling lead mask mystery of 1966"
The Cold File's coverage, "The Masks on Vintem Hill: The Lead Masks Case, 1966"

scenes.text: In August of 1966, two men were found dead on a hillside outside Rio de Janeiro, wearing formal suits and handmade lead masks over their eyes.

Manoel Pereira da Cruz and Miguel Jose Viana were electronics technicians from Campos dos Goytacazes, last seen alive by their families on 17/08/1966, heading to Niteroi for what they said was a work trip.

Three days later, a boy flying a kite on Morro do Vintem found their bodies. There were no visible wounds. Next to them was a notebook with a cryptic instruction: be at the agreed place, swallow capsules, after effect protect metals, wait for the mask signal. No capsules were ever found.
Robbery was ruled out almost immediately. Miguel had the equivalent of over a hundred thousand cruzeiros hidden in his pants, and Manoel still had cash in his jacket, both completely untouched.
By the time investigators performed the autopsy weeks later, the bodies had decomposed too far to test for poison. The actual cause of death was never determined.

The men were into radio and amateur science, which fed two competing theories: that they died during some kind of clandestine radio operation, or that they were part of a spiritist group trying to contact the dead, wearing the masks to shield their eyes from an expected blinding light. A local resident even reported a glowing orange light over the hill that same night. Neither theory has ever been proven.
Which theory do you find most convincing here -- a spiritist ritual, a radio operation gone wrong, or something else entirely?
